text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- The U.N. transitional administrator, general Jacques Klein said in an interview for Beli Manastir television that Croatian government's letter of intent represented a "good package" and nothing about it should be changed.
- Croatia has a solid military industry which offers for sale quality tanks, multiple rocket launchers, light weaponry, ammunition and auxiliary equpment.

- Why the Croats, as opposed to the Slovenes do not have a special border entrance to Austria? The problem on the horizon is that as soon as the Zagreb-Belgrade motorway is opened next summer, Croats will have to queue up with all the Balcan motorists.

- Deputy PM, Borislav Skegro said at the end of last week's seminar on liberalisation, privatisation and administration of public companies in Croatia, that the country's economic future hinges on the restructuring of public companies.

- Unexpectedly lively trading on the stock market. Big interest in the Zagrebacka Banka shares. Shareholders holding firmly onto the Adriatic pipeline (JANAF) shares are showing no intention of selling them.
- The penal code proposal to be put before the parliament envisages both husband and wife being protected against rape.

- Ownership rights are the main stumbling block in the Krsko nuclear power plant tiff between Croatia and Slovenia, says Croatian power company's representative, Kazimir Vrankic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
